p1.en: To confess or accept that something is true, often unwillingly.
p1.ex1: He admitted feeling nervous before the exam.
p1.ex2: They admitted the plan had some serious flaws.
p1.example: She finally admitted that she had made a mistake.

p1.en: In opposition to someone or something.
p1.ex1: Are you for or against the new policy?
p1.ex2: She voted against the proposal at the meeting.
p1.example: He was against the idea of moving to another city.

p1.en: Feeling relaxed and comfortable in a situation.
p1.ex1: She felt completely at ease with her new colleagues.
p1.ex2: He put the nervous guest at ease with a warm smile.
p1.example: The teacher made the students feel at ease during the test.

p1.en: To be very easy to do.
p1.ex1: Don't worry — fixing this bug will be a piece of cake.
p1.ex2: He said the job interview was a piece of cake.
p1.example: The final exam was a piece of cake for her.

p1.en: To support or agree with something.
p1.ex1: The manager is in favour of flexible working hours.
p1.ex2: Are you in favour of the new environmental policy?
p1.example: Most students are in favour of shorter school days.

p1.ru: быть на седьмом небе от счастья
p1.en: To be extremely happy and excited.
p1.ex1: He was over the moon after his team won the championship.
p1.ex2: They were over the moon to hear the good news.
p1.example: She was over the moon when she got the scholarship.

p1.en: To be in a stressful situation where you must perform or decide quickly.
p1.ex1: He works best when he is under pressure.
p1.ex2: She felt under pressure to finish the project on time.
p1.example: Teachers are often under pressure to improve test scores.

p1.en: A plan showing how much money you have and how you will spend it.
p1.ex1: They had to cut costs to stay within the budget.
p1.ex2: Planning a budget helps you avoid unnecessary spending.
p1.example: The school has a limited budget for extracurricular activities.

p1.en: To become exciting, active, or interesting.
p1.ex1: Her novel really comes to life in the final chapters.
p1.ex2: The classroom came to life when the teacher started the experiment.
p1.example: The city comes to life during the festival season.

p1.en: To think of or produce a new idea or plan.
p1.ex1: Can you come up with a better title for the essay?
p1.ex2: The team came up with an innovative marketing strategy.
p1.example: She came up with a brilliant solution to the problem.

p1.en: The ability to share information clearly and effectively with others.
p1.ex1: She improved her communication skills by joining a debate club.
p1.ex2: Employers often value strong communication skills in candidates.
p1.example: Good communication skills are essential in any workplace.

p1.en: To have power over something and manage how it works.
p1.ex1: The government aims to control inflation.
p1.ex2: You need to control the speed of the machine carefully.
p1.example: He struggled to control his emotions during the argument.

p1.en: To handle, manage, or take action regarding something.
p1.ex1: We need to deal with this issue before it gets worse.
p1.ex2: He had to deal with a lot of stress at work.
p1.example: She knows how to deal with difficult customers professionally.

p1.en: To become smaller in size, amount, or number; the act of reducing.
p1.ex1: There has been a decrease in air pollution this year.
p1.ex2: Sales decreased sharply during the economic crisis.
p1.example: The number of students decreased after the holidays.

p1.en: Requiring a lot of effort, skill, or patience.
p1.ex1: The training programme was physically demanding.
p1.ex2: She found the new role extremely demanding but rewarding.
p1.example: Being a doctor is one of the most demanding jobs in the world.

p1.en: To feel or go through something directly.
p1.ex1: He experienced a sense of achievement after completing the marathon.
p1.ex2: Many people experience stress during exam periods.
p1.example: Travellers often experience culture shock in new countries.

p1.en: Comments or reactions from others about your work or behaviour.
p1.ex1: He welcomed feedback from his colleagues to improve his performance.
p1.ex2: Please share your feedback after using the new app.
p1.example: The teacher gave the students detailed feedback on their essays.

p1.en: A sum of money saved or collected for a particular purpose.
p1.ex1: They raised a large fund to support local charities.
p1.ex2: The government allocated a special fund for education reform.
p1.example: The school set up a fund to help students buy textbooks.

p1.en: The process of increasing or developing over time.
p1.ex1: Personal growth often comes from facing challenges.
p1.ex2: Economic growth has slowed down in recent months.
p1.example: The company showed impressive growth in just one year.

p1.en: A strong effect or influence that something has on another.
p1.ex1: The new law had a positive impact on air quality.
p1.ex2: The teacher's words had a lasting impact on his students.
p1.example: Social media has had a huge impact on modern communication.

p1.en: To become or make greater in number, amount, or degree.
p1.ex1: There has been a sharp increase in online learning.
p1.ex2: Exercise can increase your energy levels significantly.
p1.example: The school fees will increase by 10% next year.

p1.en: To have an effect on how someone thinks or acts.
p1.ex1: Her parents greatly influenced her career choices.
p1.ex2: Music has the power to influence your mood.
p1.example: Advertising can strongly influence consumer behaviour.

p1.en: A feeling of excitement that gives you new ideas or motivation.
p1.ex1: She found inspiration in her grandmother's stories.
p1.ex2: The speech gave the volunteers a great deal of inspiration.
p1.example: Nature was the main inspiration behind the artist's work.

p1.en: Used to say that something is not important.
p1.ex1: 'I forgot to bring the book.' 'It doesn't matter, we have a copy.'
p1.ex2: It doesn't matter how long it takes, as long as you do it well.
p1.example: It doesn't matter if you make a mistake — just keep trying.

p1.en: Small in amount or restricted in some way.
p1.ex1: Access to clean water is still limited in some regions.
p1.ex2: The library has a limited number of books on this topic.
p1.example: We have limited time, so let's focus on the key points.

p1.en: More than half of a group.
p1.ex1: A large majority voted in favour of the new rule.
p1.ex2: The majority of people prefer to shop online these days.
p1.example: The majority of students passed the final exam.

p1.en: To move forward or improve over time.
p1.ex1: The team is making good progress on the new project.
p1.ex2: You need to make progress every day to reach your goals.
p1.example: She has made excellent progress in her English studies.

p1.en: Done by hand rather than by machine.
p1.ex1: This car has a manual gearbox.
p1.ex2: He prefers manual tools to electric ones.
p1.example: Many factories are replacing manual work with automation.

p1.en: Relating to the mind or thinking.
p1.ex1: Solving puzzles is a great mental workout.
p1.ex2: Mental strength is just as important as physical ability.
p1.example: Physical exercise can also improve your mental health.

p1.en: Less than half of a group; a small group that differs from the majority.
p1.ex1: Minority languages deserve protection and support.
p1.ex2: A small minority of people still doubt climate change.
p1.example: Only a minority of students disagreed with the new timetable.

p1.en: Used to say something is (or is not) true or factual.
p1.ex1: It's not the case that all teenagers are lazy.
p1.ex2: Many assume success is only about talent, but that's rarely the case.
p1.example: People think learning a language is difficult, but that's not always the case.

p1.en: Relating to the body rather than the mind.
p1.ex1: The job requires a lot of physical effort.
p1.ex2: She enjoys physical challenges like rock climbing.
p1.example: Physical activity is essential for a healthy lifestyle.

p1.en: To be an important part of something.
p1.ex1: Technology plays a significant role in modern healthcare.
p1.ex2: Volunteers play an important role in disaster relief efforts.
p1.word: play an important / a significant role
p1.example: Parents play an important role in their children's education.

p1.en: The ability or capacity to develop or succeed in the future.
p1.ex1: This project has great potential for growth.
p1.ex2: The teacher saw potential in even the weakest students.
p1.example: Every student has the potential to achieve great things.

p1.en: To a certain degree; more precisely.
p1.ex1: I'd rather stay home tonight than go to the party.
p1.ex2: The weather is rather cold for this time of year.
p1.example: The exam was rather difficult, but most students passed.

p1.en: To suggest that someone should do or use something.
p1.ex1: The doctor recommended that she rest for a week.
p1.ex2: Can you recommend a good restaurant nearby?
p1.example: I would recommend this book to anyone interested in history.

p1.en: To refuse to accept or approve something.
p1.ex1: His application was rejected because of missing documents.
p1.ex2: She rejected the offer and decided to start her own business.
p1.example: The committee rejected the proposal due to lack of funding.

p1.en: To write something again in a different or improved way.
p1.ex1: He decided to rewrite the entire report from scratch.
p1.ex2: After feedback, she rewrote the first paragraph completely.
p1.example: The teacher asked the student to rewrite the essay more clearly.

p1.en: The state of being protected from harm or danger.
p1.ex1: The company prioritises the safety of its employees.
p1.ex2: Wearing a helmet is important for your safety while cycling.
p1.example: Road safety is a major concern in urban areas.

p1.en: Pleased or content with something.
p1.ex1: Are you satisfied with the service you received?
p1.ex2: He was not fully satisfied with his performance.
p1.example: She was satisfied with the results of her hard work.

p1.en: A plan that shows when things will happen.
p1.ex1: She manages a very busy schedule every week.
p1.ex2: We need to adjust the schedule to meet the deadline.
p1.example: The train schedule has been updated due to roadworks.

p1.en: Important or large enough to have a noticeable effect.
p1.ex1: The discovery made a significant contribution to science.
p1.ex2: His absence had a significant impact on the team's performance.
p1.example: There has been a significant improvement in air quality.

p1.en: The place, person, or thing that something comes from.
p1.ex1: Please cite your sources at the end of the essay.
p1.ex2: Sunlight is the primary source of energy for plants.
p1.example: The internet is a major source of information today.

p1.en: To agree with and help promote an idea or person.
p1.ex1: Do you support the new school policy?
p1.ex2: She publicly supported the campaign for better public transport.
p1.example: Most of the class supported the idea of a class trip.

p1.en: To stop thinking about something by doing something else.
p1.ex1: He watched a film to take his mind off the stressful week.
p1.ex2: Listening to music helps me take my mind off worries.
p1.example: A short walk can help you take your mind off problems.

p1.en: To think in a creative and unconventional way.
p1.ex1: The project requires students to think outside the box.
p1.ex2: She always thinks outside the box when solving problems.
p1.example: Good entrepreneurs know how to think outside the box.

p1.en: During the whole period of something.
p1.ex1: She remained loyal to her team throughout the project.
p1.ex2: Throughout history, people have faced and overcome challenges.
p1.example: The company has grown significantly throughout the years.

p1.en: At any time or every time that something happens.
p1.ex1: You can call me whenever you need help.
p1.ex2: Whenever she sings, the whole room falls silent.
p1.example: Whenever I feel stressed, I go for a walk.

p1.en: Used to strongly agree with what someone has said.
p1.ex1: When she said teamwork is essential, he said he couldn't agree more.
p1.ex2: I couldn't agree more with your point about the importance of reading.
p1.example: 'Learning a second language opens many doors.' 'I couldn't agree more.'

p2.en: To plan or organise something in advance.
p2.ex1: Can you arrange a meeting for next Tuesday?
p2.ex2: He arranged all the books on the shelf alphabetically.
p2.example: She arranged a surprise party for her friend's birthday.

p2.ex1: The new campaign boosted sales by 30%.
p2.ex2: Positive feedback can boost a student's confidence significantly.
p2.example: Exercise can boost your energy and mood.

p2.en: To work together with others towards a shared goal.
p2.ex1: The two countries agreed to cooperate on environmental issues.
p2.ex2: Students cooperated well during the group presentation.
p2.example: All team members must cooperate to finish the project on time.

p2.en: The ability to analyse information carefully and make reasoned judgements.
p2.ex1: The course is designed to develop students' critical thinking skills.
p2.ex2: She used her critical thinking skills to evaluate the data.
p2.example: Critical thinking skills are vital for success in higher education.

p2.ex1: The new packaging is eco-friendly and fully recyclable.
p2.ex2: They switched to eco-friendly transport to cut emissions.
p2.example: More people are choosing eco-friendly products to reduce pollution.

p2.ex1: The museum offers a range of educational programmes for children.
p2.ex2: She prefers educational games over simple entertainment apps.
p2.example: The documentary was both entertaining and educational.

p2.en: Interesting and enjoyable to watch, listen to, or take part in.
p2.ex1: He is known for his entertaining lectures.
p2.ex2: The evening was entertaining thanks to the live music.
p2.example: The film was entertaining from start to finish.

p2.en: To create or develop something, or to come together as a group.
p2.ex1: Ice forms when water temperature drops below zero.
p2.ex2: She helped form a new environmental club at school.
p2.example: The students formed a study group before the exams.

p2.en: To communicate or work together with others.
p2.ex1: The app allows users to interact with each other in real time.
p2.ex2: She interacts confidently with both students and colleagues.
p2.example: Children learn social skills when they interact with their peers.

p2.en: Things you are required or expected to do.
p2.ex1: He took his obligations to his team very seriously.
p2.ex2: Students must be aware of their obligations regarding attendance.
p2.example: As a citizen, you have certain rights and obligations.

p2.ex1: I particularly enjoyed the last chapter of the book.
p2.ex2: The weather was particularly cold this January.
p2.example: She is particularly good at maths and science.

p2.en: To make something smaller or less in size, amount, or degree.
p2.ex1: Regular exercise helps to reduce the risk of heart disease.
p2.ex2: The company reduced its prices to attract more customers.
p2.example: We should reduce the amount of plastic we use every day.

p2.en: Giving a sense of pleasure or fulfilment.
p2.ex1: It is satisfying to finish a project you have worked hard on.
p2.ex2: She found her new job far more satisfying than the previous one.
p2.example: Helping others can be one of the most satisfying experiences.

p2.en: To spend time with other people in a friendly and relaxed way.
p2.ex1: She loves to socialise with her colleagues after work.
p2.ex2: Moving to a new city can make it harder to socialise at first.
p2.example: It's important to socialise regularly to maintain good mental health.

p2.en: For a particular purpose or in a precise way.
p2.ex1: I specifically asked for a window seat on the flight.
p2.ex2: The rules apply specifically to students in Year 10 and above.
p2.example: The course is designed specifically for advanced learners.

p2.ex1: Outdoor adventures appeal to him more than indoor activities.
p2.ex2: The design of the new phone appeals to young consumers.
p2.example: The idea of studying abroad really appeals to me.

p2.en: Used to give an example of what you have just said.
p2.ex1: There are many benefits to learning English. For instance, it improves job prospects.
p2.ex2: You can improve your health in simple ways. For instance, drink more water every day.
p2.example: Many cities have reduced pollution. For instance, Oslo banned diesel cars.
